posts.name: jffdougan
posts.cooked: I enjoyed the story part, but there was one bit of language usage that grated on me the entire time. "Prolate" is an adjective, and so the portal fiends' eyes can't be described as simply "prolates."  the missing word for what they wanted was "spheroid" - that is, the phrase "prolate spheroid."   For those who care, the variety that's squished in the other direction (flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator, like the Earth) is called an "oblate spheroid."

posts.name: dprcooke
posts.cooked:
Although deciding to call himself a luminary is certainly very consistent with his character.  Sure, he's always been Baron Blade, the hero of Mordengrad, but now he also gets to be Luminary, the guiding light who helps lead the heroes to victory against Oblivion.  He understands the nature of the threat, he understands what must be done, and he's the one best able to make sure that happens, if only the heroes would be wise enough to listen to his advice.  As far as I can tell, Blade has always considered himself to be the smartest person in the room, and choosing the name Luminary is definitely consistent with that.

Plus, there's a certain panache in taking on a hero name and then trying to out-hero the heroes, literally beating them at their own game and showing them how it's done.

I also wonder if there might also be a slight dig at Legacy in the name Luminary... Since Legacy's symbol is a lantern (i.e. source of light), I wonder if Blade went with Luminary as a subtle way of indicating that he's a better source of light.  ("Light" here being symbolic of wisdom / understanding / elightenment.)

You might be on to something there - you could certainly look at it as a dig against Legacy - Legacy literally calls back to the past whereas a Luminary would be looking forward to the future… it’s just curious to me - all the other Villain to hero name changes make a lot of sense to me (they have either Physically or mentally changed) but Baron Blade / Luminary seems pretty close to how he always was (he’s grown as a character, and he’s pragmatic enough to know that he needs to ally himself with the heroes to defeat OblivAeon and Voss) but nothing about his actions is trying to distance himself from being Baron Blade - in fact in someways he actively embraces what it means to be Baron Blade - I guess I’d have expected him to style himself as ‘Baron Blade: saviour of Earth’ or ‘Baron Blade: Hero of the Multiverse’ or something equally grand rather than taking an unrelated name that did nothing to forward his ‘brand’…
